sounds.intro: Armenian has its own alphabet with 38 letters. This pack is Eastern Armenian, the standard of Armenia. There are no genders and no articles. Stress falls on the last syllable. The Latin shown is the standard romanisation.
rows: aspirated, with a puff of air, like English "t", "p", "k", "ts", "ch"
plain, with no puff of air, like French or Spanish
a short, flat "uh", like the "a" in "about"
notes: The apostrophe marks an aspirated consonant. The plain letter is the one without the apostrophe.
Word-initial "e" and "o" are often said "ye" and "vo". The Armenian-script line is written by rule from the Latin.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Armenian often drops the pronoun, because the verb shows who is speaking. There is no he / she difference: "na" means both.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Add -er after a one-syllable word, and -ner after a longer word. After a number, the noun stays singular: erku girk' (two book).

grammar.title: To be: em, es, ê
text: "To be" is a real verb. It comes after the noun or adjective: em, es, ê, enk', ek', en.

grammar.title: Unem: have
text: Armenian says "I have": unem, unes, uni, unenk', unek', unen. "Ka" means "there is" and "chka" means "there is not".

grammar.title: Present tense: -um em
text: Verb stem + -um + a form of "to be". Utel (to eat): utum em, utum es, utum ê.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Order: who, where or when, what, verb. Armenian has no articles: "girk'" means "a book" or "the book".

grammar.title: Negation
text: Replace "em" with "ch'em", "es" with "ch'es", and so on. "Ch'ka" means "there is not".
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: A yes or no question uses the same words as the statement, with a rising voice on the word you ask about.

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stand just before the verb.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Put the word before the noun: im (my), k'o (your), nra (his / her), mer (our), dzer (your, formal), nrants' (their). To like something, say "it pleases me": indz dur ê galis.

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: du (informal): friends, family, children. duk' (formal): strangers, older people, work. The verb changes: es (informal), ek' (formal).

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: The past adds -ts' or -ets' to the stem (gnats'i, I went). The future puts k- in front of the present: kgnam (I will go).

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: the short form (ari). Formal: add -k' (arek'). To forbid, put "mi" in front.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Can: karogh em + verb. Must: petk' ê + verb. Want: uzum em + verb.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Armenian uses endings and small words after the noun: -um (in), -i vra (on), -i mot (near), -its' (from), -in (to).
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Put "aveli" before the adjective for "more": aveli mets. For "the most" use "amenaveli": amenaveli mets. "Than" is "k'an".
ex: sa aveli lav ê k'an ayn
sah ah-veh-LEE lahv ê kahn ayn
սա ավելի լավ է քան այն
sa aveli vat ê k'an ayn
sah ah-veh-LEE vaht ê kahn ayn
սա ավելի վատ է քան այն
T'ashk'endə aveli mets ê k'an Samarkandə
tahsh-ken-DUH ah-veh-LEE mets ê kahn sah-mahr-kahn-DUH
թաշքենդը ավելի մեծ է քան սամարկանդը
